s: In-memory data structure store serving as cache, session store, rate limiter, and pub/sub backbone at microsecond latency.
w: Single-threaded event loop handles commands; data structures (strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams) serve diverse use cases. RDB/AOF persistence provides durability options; replication with Sentinel or Cluster provides HA and sharding. Lua scripts execute atomic operations; TTLs expire keys automatically. Redis Streams compete with Kafka for lightweight eventing.
use: Caching layer absorbing DB reads with sub-millisecond response times
Session storage for authenticated user state across stateless API instances
Distributed locking (Redlock) and rate limiting (sliding window counters)
Real-time leaderboards and counters using sorted sets and atomic increments
Lightweight pub/sub for inter-service notifications (Redis Streams preferred at scale)
avoid: Primary data store without persistence (Redis is optimized for speed not durability)
Datasets exceeding available RAM (Redis is in-memory by design)
Complex relational queries - Redis is not a relational database

props.max_memory_policy: How Redis evicts when full: allkeys-lru, volatile-lru, noeviction

pat.d: App checks Redis first, misses go to DB then populate Redis.
Sorted set sliding window or token bucket in Lua script for atomic rate enforcement.

pits: Cache stampede on hot key expiry - use locking (SETNX) or stale-while-revalidate
Memory limit hit with allkeys-lru evicting critical keys - use volatile-lru with TTL discipline
Cluster mode sharding misunderstandings - key design must account for hash slot routing
tips: Redis data structures are the interview differentiator: sorted sets for leaderboards, streams for events, Lua for atomic scripts
Redis Cluster vs Sentinel: Cluster for sharding, Sentinel for HA of a single dataset
